panels.description: Request success rate. 99.5% or higher is healthy (green); below 98% is critical (red). Only normally completed requests with finished_reason='stop' are counted as successful.
panels.title: Success Rate

panels.description: Number of requests currently running plus waiting. A sharp increase indicates a traffic spike.
panels.title: Active Requests

panels.description: Scheduler efficiency: Running / (Running + Waiting). At 100%, every request is processed immediately. Below 70% indicates overload.
panels.title: System Efficiency

panels.description: P99 time to first token. This is the key measure of the initial response speed experienced by users. Under 1 second is ideal.
panels.title: TTFT P99

panels.description: [Critical] Preemption rate. Requests in progress are interrupted when the KV cache is exhausted. Investigate immediately if this is above 0. Consider adding GPU memory or reducing the batch size.
panels.title: Preemption Rate

panels.description: Total time from receiving a request to completing its response. P50 means half of requests finish within this time; P99 means 99% do. A sharp increase in P99 warrants bottleneck analysis.
panels.title: E2E Request Latency

panels.description: Share of latency spent in prefill (input processing) versus decode (output generation). High prefill latency points to long input prompts; high decode latency points to long generated outputs.
panels.title: Inference Stage Breakdown

panels.description: Comparison of TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT (time per output token). High TTFT indicates a prefill bottleneck; high TPOT indicates a decode bottleneck.
panels.title: TTFT vs TPOT

panels.description: Tokens processed per second. Input (Prompt) represents input tokens; Output (Generation) represents generated tokens. Higher throughput indicates better system efficiency.
panels.title: Token Throughput

panels.description: Ratio of input tokens to output tokens. A high ratio indicates long inputs and short outputs (RAG); a low ratio indicates short inputs and long outputs (generation or summarization).
panels.title: Token I/O Ratio

panels.description: Percentage of computation saved by the prefix cache. Higher values mean the cache skips more prefill computation and saves GPU resources. Calculated as (1 - actual computation / total input) * 100.
panels.title: Prefix Cache Savings

panels.description: Distribution of input (prompt) token counts per request. Darker colors indicate more requests of that length. If requests cluster in a particular range, consider optimizing for that length.
panels.title: Request Length Heatmap (Prompt)

panels.description: Time requests spend waiting in the queue. Queue time increases when the GPU is busy. If it remains high, consider scaling out to additional instances.
panels.title: Request Queue Time

panels.description: GPU KV cache utilization. This memory stores intermediate computation results. Use caution above 80%; above 95% carries a risk of preemption.
panels.title: GPU KV Cache Usage

panels.description: Prefix cache hit rate: the proportion of requests that reuse the same system prompt or few-shot examples. A rate of 70% or higher is efficient and is a key metric in RAG environments.
panels.title: Prefix Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Request count by scheduler state. Running means inference on the GPU, Waiting means queued, and Swapped means swapped out of memory. A sustained increase in Waiting indicates overload.
panels.title: Scheduler State

panels.description: Python garbage-collection events and process memory usage. Frequent GC or steadily increasing RSS may indicate a memory leak.
panels.title: Python GC & Memory

panels.description: Distribution of request completion reasons. stop means normal completion (EOS), length means the maximum length was reached, and abort means the request was interrupted. A high abort rate indicates a problem.
panels.title: Finish Reason Distribution

panels.description: Total request throughput versus successful requests over time. A gap indicates failed requests; the two should consistently match during normal operation.
panels.title: Throughput vs Success
